item.title: Comparing quantized backends
item.description:
Our first benchmark post put Nox 3.2× ahead of ComfyUI on an RTX 4080. After it went up, the ComfyUI team kindly told us to run with --use-ck-attention on CUDA 13+, which enables their new Comfy Kitchen attention backend. ComfyUI’s warm times in our benchmark dropped by 2.5× to 3.4× on average, depending on the GPU.

Mean warm speedup, Nox over ComfyUI Before After
RTX 3090, Low 3.00× 1.11×
RTX 3090, High 2.67× 1.00×
RTX 4080, Low 3.21× 1.23×
RTX 4080, High 3.40× 1.17×
RTX 5090, Low 2.98× 1.87×
RTX 5090, High 2.63× 1.31×
H100, Low 4.84× 1.54×
H100, High 4.11× 1.31×

Each value is the mean of the per-pipeline speedups over all 16 pipelines. The full tables are on the RTX 3090, RTX 4080, RTX 5090 and H100 pages.

item.title: Nox sparse attention against SpargeAttn
item.description:
This is a follow-up to our sparse attention post. That post introduced Nox sparse attention, attention mass and the Laplacian loss. Since then we added SpargeAttn to Nox as a second sparse attention backend. We compared the two on a MiniMax-H3 I2V render and found that one setting decides more of the result than the routers themselves: how a router treats the text and conditioning tokens.

We use the same setup as the distilled checkpoint comparison and its rally car I2V shot.

item.title: Faster MiniMax-H3 with Sage and Sparse Attention
item.description:
MiniMax-H3 generates video and audio together, and due to its large model size it is the most attention-heavy model in our lineup. Attention is well known to be the most expensive part of inference: attention grows with the square of the token count.

In this post we follow two changes to the attention of MiniMax-H3. Warm measurements on RTX 4080:

1344×768, 124 frames, I2V Wall time Denoise Speedup vs Nox cuDNN
Nox, cuDNN 147.8s 128.1s –
Nox, SageAttention 84.3s 64.5s 1.75×
Nox, Sage + 15% raster routing 66.7s 46.8s 2.22×
Nox, Sage + 15% Nox sparse 66.7s 46.7s 2.22×
Nox, Sage + Veda 44 tiles 68.1s 47.9s 2.17×

Quantizing the kernel with SageAttention

MiniMax-H3 has 1344×768 as its official 16:9 canvas. At that shape, cuDNN flash attention is close to the FP16 Tensor Core roof. SageAttention takes a different route: it keeps attention dense, but moves QKᵀ to INT8 and P·V to FP8. The lower-precision Tensor Core paths have a much higher throughput roof on Ada.

item.title: Benchmarking Nox against ComfyUI
item.description:
Update: we’ve since rerun the benchmark with ComfyUI’s Comfy Kitchen backend. See the new benchmark post for the current numbers.

A speedup is only meaningful if both sides did the same work. It is easy to make an inference engine look fast: run fewer steps, drop to a lower resolution, swap in a smaller or more aggressively quantized checkpoint, or compare a warm process against a cold one. We wanted the Nox benchmarks to be immune to all of that, so this post explains how the comparison is set up and then shows every output from the latest run next to its ComfyUI counterpart.
